name: BGE-M3

lineage.how_derived: unsupervised contrastive pretraining then unified fine-tuning for dense, sparse and multi-vector retrieval

purpose: One multilingual embedder that does dense, sparse (lexical) and ColBERT-style multi-vector retrieval over inputs from short sentences to 8192-token documents in 100+ languages (card).

license.name: MIT
license.notes: Card tag mit; the HF repo has no LICENSE file, so text not read. HF createdAt 2024-01-27.

architecture.why_this_design: Multi-Functionality, Multi-Linguality, Multi-Granularity (title of the paper, arXiv 2402.03216): the three retrieval modes share one model and can be fused for hybrid ranking.

variants.notes: llama.cpp dense only; sparse and ColBERT outputs need FlagEmbedding

pc-16gb.notes: runs beside the coder, or on CPU

engine_support.notes: llama.cpp serves the dense vector only.

benchmarks.name: PosIR / aggregate multilingual retrieval vs Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B

strengths: dense plus sparse plus multi-vector in one model
weaknesses: older (Jan 2024): Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B scores higher on aggregate multilingual and code retrieval in the independent tables found
best_for: multilingual document search where hybrid dense plus lexical ranking is wanted
avoid_for: code retrieval where Qwen3-Embedding is available

user_reports.summary: Korean practice guide: bge-m3 has the more mature retrieval tooling; Qwen3 performs best when each query carries a one-sentence task instruction.

soft.maturity: BAAI, very large community, many quants; no update since 2024.

tona_fit.reason: MIT, tiny and mature, and the only one here with a native sparse plus multi-vector mode, but Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B is newer and ahead on code and aggregate retrieval at similar size; keep as the hybrid-search alternative.
